In this post we're gonna write Wazuh detection rules and test them in real-time simulated attack.
We have three machines that I will use and refer to during this lab, the attacker machine, the Wazuh agent that also runs Suricata engine and the Wazuh server where I write rules at as illustrated in the whiteboard below.

![Pasted image 20261116152631](assets/images/task11-write-custom-wazuh-detection-rules/Pasted%20image%2020261116152631.png)

## 1. Detect NMAP SYN scan

First, add detection rule to suricata's custom rules file in /etc/suricata/rules/local.rule.

Rule:
```
alert tcp any any -> $HOME_NET any (msg:"POSSIBLE NMAP SCAN DETECTED WINDOW 1024"; flow:stateless; flags:S; window:1024; priority:3; classtype:attempted-recon; sid:1000000; rev:1;)
```
The flag 'S' is for tracking SYN packets only.

Source: [amvatlabs.com](https://www.amvatlabs.com/posts/014-SynScanBehaviourIDSDetection/).

![](data:image/png;base64,)

And restart suricata service.

Second, add detection rule of the repeated occurrence within a specific time range of suricata's previous rule above to detect when automatic TCP SYN requests are sent to many ports on the monitored endpoint.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Shown above two rules, one which monitors and second that detects the occurrence using frequency and timeframe fields in \`&lt;rule id="100511" level="12" frequency="15" timeframe="10"&gt;\`.

Then, reload or restart the Wazuh manager to apply them.

Third, Trigger the alert using NMAP from a third machine to the \`raneem-agent-1\` monitored endpoint as shown below.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

And it fires the alerts of rule ID 100510 and ID 100511 that we wrote above, and the description: "POSSIBLE NMAP SCAN DETECTED WINDOW 1024" as shown below in the dashboard screen.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

In the end, this rule proves that a single source sent too many TCP SYN requests to many destination ports but it doesn't detect the tool was NMAP and doesn't distinguish wither it's a DDoS attack or port scan, also doesn't identify port scan by many IPs.

## 2. Detect brute-force attack and failed login attempts

Let's write a Wazuh rule to local_rules.xml as shown below.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

If rule ID 5760 is triggered, which is failure login attempts for SSH with some conditions (same source IP, target user and target agent/endpoint) within a specified time window, then the custom rules 100006 and 100007 are fired.

To test it, I'll start a bruteforce attack using Hydra tool in my attacker machine as shown below.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

And the alert of a bruteforce attack is triggered as shown below.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Alert key values:
- Time: Nov 3, 2026 @ 19:01
- Rule description: Brute-force attack detected from 192.168.230.130 targeting root. 
- Rule ID: 100007
